programmes.t: Weapons That Changed the World
programmes.d: Today’s infantry demands a weapon combining machine gun firepower with rifle accuracy and mobility.. Host Wil Willis traces this journey through iconic firearms.

programmes.t: WWII's The Great Escapes: The Freedom Trails: Italy: The Sulmona Trail
programmes.d: Monty follows the route taken by prisoner of war Len Harley, who spent months on the run before braving snow, ice, and Nazi patrols to escape over the mountains of the Majella in Italy.

programmes.t: The Rise of the Nazi Party: Nazis Outfought
programmes.d: By 1944, Hitler's image as a victorious leader is crumbling. He faces a bomb plot led by Stauffenberg and Tresckow, intending to kill him and overthrow the regime. Hitler survives the bombing, triggering a brutal reprisal against conspirators.

programmes.t: Secret War: The Special Interrogation Group
programmes.d: The SIG consisted of German speaking Jewish volunteers from Palestine. They had a highly dangerous job: which was to pose as Germans behind enemy lines and extract intelligence and do acts of sabotage. Few had a long-life expectancy.

programmes.t: Weapons That Changed the World
programmes.d: Could the mighty M2 be the greatest machine gun in history? Nicknamed “Ma Deuce”, this American machine gun has dominated battlefields for over 80 years. Host Wil Willis tests it and recreates Audie Murphy’s famous Medal of Honor moment.

programmes.t: WWII's The Great Escapes: The Freedom Trails: Italy: Operation Galia
programmes.d: Monty’s journey sees him follow the path 33 SAS soldiers took after they were parachuted behind enemy lines to attack the enemy and create chaos to draw Nazi-fascist forces away from the front line.

programmes.t: Auschwitz: The Nazis and the Final Solution: Factories of Death
programmes.d: Året 1942 bliver det mest betydningsfulde i "den Endelige Løsning", da nazisterne begynder at gennemrode Vesteuropa og endda tager jøder fra så fjerne steder som de britiske kanaløer.

programmes.t: Weapons That Changed the World
programmes.d: They are iconic weapons: the Tommy Gun, Uzi, and today’s MP5. Invented to break WWI stalemates, the submachine gun revolutionized warfare and culture. Host Wil Willis explores its evolution, firing the Thompson and BAR.

programmes.t: Secret War: The Spymistress and the French Fiasco
programmes.d: After WWII, SOE disbanded, leaving Vera Atkins to uncover fates of 118 agents, including 13 women. Many were betrayed and sent to camps; some were executed. Atkins' quest continued, marked by personal impact and delayed recognition.

programmes.t: Nazi Collaborators: The IRA Conspiracy
programmes.d: During WWII, the IRA's "S Plan" aimed to bomb Britain, drawing German support to weaken the British. "Operation Green" and "Plan Kathleen" envisioned IRA aiding a German invasion of Northern Ireland, but both failed due to bungling and infighting.

programmes.t: Nazi Collaborators: The Jews Who Fought for Hitler
programmes.d: In Hitler’s Germany, those with Jewish ancestry faced harsh Nuremberg Laws. Full Jews faced death; Mischlinge endured discrimination, job bans. Some, like Helmut Schmidt, unaware of heritage, found protectors like Milch in high places.

programmes.t: The Rise of the Nazi Party: End Game
programmes.d: In January 1945, Nazi Germany faces defeat as Allied armies close in. Hitler, aged 55 and in poor health, remains defiant in his Berlin bunker. On April 30th, 1945, Hitler commits suicide, and days later, Germany surrenders, ending World War II.

programmes.t: Secret War: Agent Garbo
programmes.d: Juan Pujol, MI6's WWII agent "Garbo," created a fictitious spy network in Lisbon, deceiving the Germans with crucial disinformation and influencing their strategies. After the war, MI6 protected him, and he lived in Venezuela until his death in 1988.

programmes.t: Nazi Collaborators: The Arajs Kommando
programmes.d: Viktor Arajs, a Latvian, played a significant role in the Holocaust, collaborating with the Nazis to eliminate Jews. Leading the Arajs Kommando, he orchestrated the killings of around 30,000 Jews. Arajs justified his actions as patriotic defense.

programmes.t: The Rise of the Nazi Party: Preparing for War
programmes.d: Hitler unveils his military plans: annex Austria, seize the Sudetenland, and eventually invade Poland and the Soviet Union. By March 1938, Austria falls bloodlessly. By September 1939, he invades Poland, sparking World War Two.

programmes.t: WWII's The Great Escapes: The Freedom Trails: Slovenia: The Crow's Flight
programmes.d: Monty heads to Slovenia to retrace one of the most daring, yet unknown, mass escapes of Allied prisoners during the second world war, made possible only with the help of partisans and locals.

programmes.t: Weapons That Changed the World
programmes.d: Former U.S. Army Ranger Wil Willis tests modern combat shotguns like the Benelli M4 and Mossberg 590, alongside historic models.This documentary features 3D animations and weapon tests to explore effectiveness of combat shotguns.

programmes.t: The Rise of the Nazi Party: In Power
programmes.d: Adolf Hitler's secret agenda is to rid Germany of Jews. By 1938, after creating work schemes and rearming, he orchestrates "The Night of Broken Glass," burning 1,000 synagogues and killing 91 Jews, preparing for further aggression.

programmes.t: Nazi Collaborators: Hitler's Killer Police
programmes.d: In Ukraine and Lithuania, Nazi invaders were welcomed as liberators. In Lithuania, Antanas Gecas led a militia that executed hundreds of Jews. Ukrainian nationalists participated in pogroms slaughtering 34,000 Jews in two days.

programmes.t: Signs of Evil - The Runes of the SS
programmes.d: The symbol of the SS stands for terror and the murder of millions. Documentary about the history of a symbol that represents murder.

programmes.t: Secret War: Christine Granville
programmes.d: Christine Granville, aka Krystyna Skarbek, a brave SOE agent, secured the release of captured comrades from the Gestapo before Operation Dragoon, earning the George Medal.

programmes.t: The Rise of the Nazi Party: Becoming Respectable
programmes.d: In 1924, Hitler is convicted for High Treason after the failed Nazi power grab. In prison, he writes Mein Kampf, articulating his anti-Semitic and expansionist beliefs. Upon release, Hitler rebrands the Nazi Party.

programmes.t: The Real Oppenheimer
programmes.d: I 1945 blev verden ført ind i atomalderen. Da hans rolle som bombens fader var blevet cementeret, blev Oppenheimer mere og mere bekymret over den potentielle fare, som videnskabelige opfindelser kunne udgøre for menneskeheden.

programmes.t: Hitler Uncovering His Fatal Obsession: Barbarossa Unleashed 1941
programmes.d: E1 begins with a brief examination of the rationale of hatred projected by Hitler onto the Soviet-Slavic-Jewish world. Then it leaps forward, to see Hitler initiate an invasion of the USSR.
